_description: Sector-relative IV baselines for options timing. Updated from historical IV distributions. IV rank thresholds are sector-specific because tech naturally runs higher IV than utilities/staples.
_methodology: Baselines derived from 252-day rolling IV distributions per sector ETF and constituent stocks. 'expensive_rank' is the IV rank level that is genuinely elevated FOR THAT SECTOR (not a flat 70% cutoff). 'cheap_rank' is where IV is genuinely cheap for that sector.

XLK.name: Technology
XLK.notes: Tech naturally runs high IV due to growth/momentum. IV rank 65% is normal, not expensive. Only penalize above 80%.

XLV.name: Healthcare
XLV.notes: Healthcare is defensive with moderate IV. Rank above 65% is genuinely elevated.

XLF.name: Financials
XLF.notes: Financials are low-vol. IV rank 60% is already expensive for this sector.

XLE.name: Energy
XLE.notes: Energy has commodity-driven vol spikes. Moderate baseline.

XLU.name: Utilities
XLU.notes: Utilities are the lowest-vol sector. IV rank 55% is already elevated. Current IV=46 is unusually high due to rate environment.

XLP.name: Consumer Staples
XLP.notes: Staples are very low-vol defensive. Similar to utilities — low threshold for expensive.

XLY.name: Consumer Discretionary
XLY.notes: Discretionary has moderate-high vol due to AMZN/TSLA weighting. Tolerates higher IV rank.

XLB.name: Materials
XLB.notes: Materials are commodity-sensitive cyclicals, moderate vol.

XLRE.name: Real Estate
XLRE.notes: Real estate is rate-sensitive with low baseline vol.

XLC.name: Communication Services
XLC.notes: Communication dominated by META/GOOG — moderate-high vol profile similar to tech-lite.

penalty_schedule._description: Sector-relative confidence penalty for options buying. Penalty is applied when IV rank exceeds the sector-specific 'expensive_rank' threshold. Penalty scales linearly from 0% at threshold to max_penalty at IV rank 100%.
